content.value_statement: Expo apps often need native device features with careful permissions and platform handling. This skill provides focused patterns for adding camera, notifications, haptics, location, storage, app state, and keyboard behavior.
actual_capabilities: Shows permission request and status patterns for camera, media, notifications, and location.
Provides Expo camera and image picker workflows for capture and gallery selection.
Outlines push notification registration, local scheduling, receiving, response handling, and backend sending.
Covers haptic feedback patterns for taps, confirmations, errors, and picker selection.
Explains location reads, location watching, local storage, SecureStore, app state, and keyboard handling.
limitations: Examples are snippets, not a complete runnable app.
Expo SDK and package versions must be checked in the target project.
iOS and Android permission wording still needs product and store review.
Backend notification examples require secure token handling outside the skill.

use_cases.title: Permission-first camera flow
use_cases.description: Add camera capture or gallery selection while handling granted, denied, and not-yet-requested states.

use_cases.title: Push notification rollout
use_cases.description: Plan Expo push token registration, local reminders, foreground behavior, tap handling, and backend sending.

use_cases.title: Native capability review
use_cases.description: Check location, haptics, secure storage, app lifecycle, and keyboard patterns before implementation.

prompt_templates.title: Add camera permission
prompt_templates.prompt: Use rn-native-features to add camera permission handling for an Expo React Native screen. Explain the states before showing code.

prompt_templates.title: Create image capture flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Use rn-native-features to design an Expo image capture and gallery selection flow. Include permission handling, editing options, and user feedback.

prompt_templates.title: Implement notifications
prompt_templates.prompt: Use rn-native-features to implement push notification registration, foreground handling, tap responses, and a secure backend sending plan for Expo.

prompt_templates.title: Audit native integration
prompt_templates.prompt: Use rn-native-features to review my Expo native feature plan for permission gaps, device-only constraints, storage choices, and testing steps.

output_examples.input: Add camera support to my profile screen.
output: Permission request flow before rendering the camera.
Fallback copy for denied camera access.
Photo capture approach with quality and metadata choices.

output_examples.input: Prepare Expo push notifications for a beta release.
output: Foreground notification and tap-response handling steps.
Backend sending responsibilities and token safety notes.

output_examples.input: Choose storage for preferences and auth tokens.
output: SecureStore recommendation for tokens and credentials.

best_practices: Request and check permissions before rendering native controls.
Test camera, haptics, location, and notifications on physical devices.
Use SecureStore for tokens and AsyncStorage only for non-sensitive preferences.
anti_patterns: Skipping denied-permission states and showing a blank native feature screen.
Treating push notification payload routes as trusted without validation.
Using SecureStore for large documents or general cache data.

faq.question: Does this skill write a complete Expo app?
faq.answer: No. It provides implementation patterns and snippets that must be adapted to the target project.

faq.question: Does it cover Android behavior?
faq.answer: It mainly targets Expo React Native APIs and includes some platform notes. Project-specific Android testing is still required.

faq.question: Can it send push notifications by itself?
faq.answer: No. It shows client registration, local scheduling, and a backend request pattern for Expo Push API.

faq.question: Does it handle permissions automatically?
faq.answer: No. It explains how to request permissions and respond to denied access.

faq.question: Can it store sensitive tokens?
faq.answer: It recommends Expo SecureStore for tokens and credentials. Large data should use other storage.

faq.question: Should I test on a simulator?
faq.answer: Some features work in simulators, but camera, haptics, and push notifications often require a physical device.
